input: nums is a dense Array of integer Number values and k is an integer Number. Zero, negative values and repeated prefix sums are supported; an empty Array returns 0. Every input, k, every mathematical prefix sum and every prefix minus k must lie in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. The maximum possible count n * (n + 1) / 2 must be <= 9007199254740991. These are mathematical domain conditions, not floating-point checks performed by the candidate. Signed zero is treated as integer zero. NaN, infinities, BigInt, non-integers and sparse arrays are outside the domain. Inputs are not validated.
return: Type: nonnegative safe-integer Number. Exact integer equality for the number of nonempty contiguous subarrays with sum k. Invariants: counts starts with the empty prefix 0 occurring once. After adding each value, query counts[prefix - k] before incrementing counts[prefix], so the current prefix cannot count as an empty subarray. All prior occurrences of an equal prefix remain counted; the algorithm does not assume positive inputs.
mutation_aliasing: Input mutation: none. scalar result No persistent Solution instance state.
numeric: Exact safe-integer Number arithmetic within the stated prefix, difference and count bounds; no bitwise coercions. On the shared domain, every input, k, every mathematical prefix and every prefix minus k lies in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], and n * (n + 1) / 2 <= 9007199254740991.
